Execution trace: AutoTranslate.preview_judge_scope selects first N per translation (autotranslate.py:741-773), BatchAutoTranslate globally decrements remaining cap across translations sorted component/language/pk (autotranslate.py:1240-1270). For each translation process_judge optionally MT-pretranslates writable IDs, then one run_judge_batch (autotranslate.py:832-902). run_judge_batch resolves both profiles, selected seats default (1,2), computes initial_paid_calls=sum(ceil(len(pending)/profile[seat].batch_size)); validates/caches each unit; _run_seats launches one thread per seat with same ordered requests, and barrier persists each batch before releasing corresponding seat (judge_loop.py:1320-1430, 1119-1238). Static preview count = sum ceil(strings/batch_size) (judge.py:815-830); defaults batch=5, seat overrides inherit global (defaults.py:61-70,87-89; settings_docker.py:1745-1797). Thus 2000 units, both seats batch 5 => 400+400=800 clean initial POSTs, not ~3000.

Actual outbound attempts per batch are not 1: judge.py:_run_batch (1770-1948) sends primary, retries transport/http transient/protocol according to JUDGE_*_RETRIES (defaults each 1), auth 401/403 adds exactly one fallback POST (fallback never retried), failover kinds can fallback once; multi-item parser failures trigger width-1 isolation, each unit recursively POSTed (fallback not multiplied in isolation); shared RetryBudget=max ceil(initial_paid_calls*JUDGE_RETRY_BUDGET_RATIO), default ratio .2, consumed by retry and isolation. request_verdicts re-reads adaptive seat batch budget before each batch; adaptive state can shrink profile batch after transport/deadline and persist across runs (judge.py:1944-2085; adaptive funcs ~1590-1640). Therefore effective requests = sum over rounds/seats/batches of primary POST + permitted retries + fallback + parser isolation, not simply ceil(N/5).

Rounds: run_judge_batch has unparsed retry rounds (default 1) only when every selected seat has unparsed rows, potentially another 2-seat pass; repair attempt loop max JUDGE_MAX_REPAIR_ATTEMPTS (default 1). For writable defect, repair_targets calls project routed MT (batch engine fetch_machinery_matches or per-unit if engine.batch_size==1; judge_loop.py:184-267), then changed units are rejudged in next pending round. Candidate/proposal path: each candidate is stored, then recursively run_judge_batch([unit], writable_ids=set(), candidate_targets=..., same selected seats), causing up to 2 more judge POSTs/unit; proposal-only disables MT/state-mutating repair (autotranslate.py:832-900). Producer proposal/recheck callers explicitly set proposal_only=True, pretranslate=False, mutating_repairs=False (api/producer/views.py:164-167,261-265; tasks.py:1711-1739). Deferral drain uses single selected seat, use_cache=False, bounded seat capacity (judge_loop.py:1950-1985).

Cache key is request_identity built from unit id, target hash, context hash (source/note/explanation/glossary/clarification), project_context hash, source/target languages, profile_fingerprint, prompt schema; _cached_verdict requires complete parsed rows for BOTH seats and exact model, and cache only applies when selected seats are both seats (judge_loop.py around _cached_verdict; run batch 1360-1410). Any target/context/profile/alias revision/prompt schema change invalidates. Concurrent redelivery: process_judge excludes already_done only non-PENDING JudgeRunUnit; simultaneous workers can both see PENDING and pay. _adopt_producer_run row lock does not mutex already RUNNING same task ID; saved investigation confirms duplicate runs/overlap hypothesis.

Exact formula for one invocation: Let R be repair/rejudge rounds; for each round r and seat s, E_rs=ceil(U_rs / B_eff_rs), where B_eff is adaptive current budget (<= configured batch), and each batch b has A=1 primary + T transport retries + H transient HTTP retries + P protocol retries, bounded by shared retry budget/deadline; + F fallback (at most 1 on auth/failover); + I parser isolation unit calls (only failed multi-item batches, budgeted). Add U_unparsed_retry extra rounds (only all-seat unparsed), and recursive candidate rejudge calls (each 2-seat, usually width 1). Repair MT calls are separate provider calls, not JudgeRequestAttempt; JudgeRequestAttempt/LLMUsageLog only count judge HTTP attempts. 3004/3031 vs 800 implies ~3.75 attempts/clean initial slot; plausible contributors are adaptive B_eff collapse + retries/fallback/isolation and duplicated/redelivered execution, but cannot attribute without per-attempt batch_size/attempt ordinal/failure_kind/round/subject and timing. Recorded Anvil data says repaired=0, but this does NOT rule out failed/empty repair MT; 10 unparsed second run supports retry/deferred paths only as possibility, not proof.

Exact aggregation fields: JudgeRequestAttempt model (trans/models/judge.py:434-530): run FK, created_at, seat, attempt ordinal, provider, endpoint_fingerprint, model/model_fingerprint/profile_fingerprint/prompt_schema_version, batch_digest, batch_size, transport_succeeded, parsed, failure_kind, http_status, exception_class, finish_reason, response_shape, response_segment_count, elapsed_ms, first_byte_ms, response_bytes, prompt/completion/total/reasoning tokens, response_id. Group by run+seat+attempt ordinal+failure_kind+batch_size; count distinct batch_digest and sum elapsed only for attempts (never wall-clock sum). Join LLMUsageLog (trans/models/llm_usage.py:31-130) via request_attempt/run: created_at, service/model, project/component snapshots, target_language_code, prompt/completion/total/reasoning/cached tokens, cost_usd (null=unpriced), unit_count, batch_size, outcome/refusal_reason. JudgeRunUnit (judge.py model lines 690-794): run/unit snapshot, translation/component/project, outcome/skip_reason, verdict, repair_status, initial/final severity, attempt_count, cached, candidate hashes/ids, projection_succeeded. JudgeVerdict lines 795-930: unit, seat, attempt (repair cycle), request_round (transport recovery), subject live/candidate, target/context/profile/prompt hashes, request_attempt FK, provider/model, unparsed. These fields permit exact decomposition by round, subject, seat, provider, batch width, parsed/failure, tokens/cost. Also aggregate JudgeAdaptiveState (judge.py model ~510-560): endpoint/model/seat batch_budget, clean streak, failure streak/circuit state; it explains adaptive effective-width changes.

Arithmetic nuance: 3000 JudgeRequestAttempt rows/run over 2000 units is 3000 POSTs, versus 800 clean static batches (400 per seat). If every selected unit got one call per seat, observed avg effective batch width = (2*2000)/3000 ≈1.33 requests' worth (before extra retries/fallback); adaptive seat budget collapse from 5→2→1 is a code-supported mechanism (transport/deadline halves shared JudgeAdaptiveState budget, never exceeds profile; judge.py adaptive funcs). But this is not proof adaptive caused it: concurrent redelivery can duplicate work while PENDING, and retries/fallback/unparsed rounds add attempts. Need production query timeline by attempt created_at and batch_size + adaptive state history (only current state stored) to separate.

Fresh B1=2/B2=1 fully explains ~3000 clean initial POSTs: E_initial=ceil(2000/2)+ceil(2000/1)=1000+2000=3000, exactly matching attempts; prior 800 baseline assumed inherited B=5 and is superseded. Seat override names are JUDGE_BATCH_SIZE_SEAT_1/2 and config snapshots/attempts prove production values. No need invoke adaptive/retry hypotheses for Anvil clean-count; still report retries separately but clean 3000 is expected.

_barrier current code uses coverage end_offset (judge_loop.py _run_seats ~1160-1238), not same batch index. With B1=2 and B2=1: seat1 event [0,2] and seat2 [0,1] persist; seat2 cannot ack until peer coverage>=1; once seat1 [0,2] is persisted, seat2 [0,1] releases, then seat2 [1,2] may run; seat1 [0,2] releases only when seat2 coverage>=2. This lets seat2 finish requests covering up to seat1's current end offset (not race ahead beyond it), while seat1 waits. Then seat1 [2,4] can be pending while seat2 [2,3],[3,4] catch up; bounded look-ahead is <= peer event end_offset, but unequal widths create multiple seat2 POSTs per seat1 event. Fatal peer errors release all pending/future events via _SeatAbortedError. Recommendation: do not claim a strict same-batch-index barrier; describe coverage/end-offset barrier. For cost optimization, equalize seat batch widths only if quality/latency permits (e.g. both 2 or 5), because B2=1 deterministically doubles seat2 request count and fixed prompt overhead; however changing overrides needs evaluation/approval and may alter provider behavior. Keep independent seat models if quality requires, and measure tokens/latency before widening.

Findings (read-only): payload is weblate/trans/judge.py:879-935,1624-1690. Every HTTP request repeats full verdict.txt system prompt; schema JSON is rebuilt per batch (`minItems=maxItems=batch size`) and user JSON repeats boundary + warning + all segments. Random token_hex boundary inserted immediately before segments, potentially harms provider prefix-cache beyond stable warning. No neighbor/context duplication: each request segment only key/source/target, optional rendered pair, note/explanation/clarification, full matched glossary, failing checks; prompt explicitly says one segment, no unseen conventions. `_segment` lines 901-934; no neighbors. Glossary source weblate/glossary/models.py:407-475: matched full=True/include_variants=True, excludes not-applicable/untranslated non-readonly, serializes source/target + both explanations + flags; dedup only exact serialized entry. Thus glossary variants/explanations/flags can dominate input and are per-segment repeated, but scope is source-match, not project-wide. `forms.py:704-716` explanation max 1000 chars; clarification also sent if present. Checks are only names (`failing_checks` list), no descriptions (judge rules say don't repeat deterministic checks). Outputs require every segment id/verdict/errors/back_translation (`judge.py:883-903`), and prompt demands whole back_translation + English descriptions (`verdict.txt` lines ~74-123); errors can be verbose/unbounded except provider max_tokens. `defaults.py:72-79`: default reasoning empty, json_schema, stream false, temperature 0, max_tokens 0 means no output limit. Usage/accounting: `_write_llm_usage` `judge.py:1464-1513` records provider prompt/completion/total, nested prompt cached_tokens, nested completion reasoning_tokens, provider cost; silently skips row when both prompt/completion absent. `total_tokens` fallback prompt+completion; no local tokenizer, no per-field breakdown, no prompt hash/bytes, no cache eligibility/hit type, no input/output/reasoning prices. `LLMUsageLog` model `weblate/trans/models/llm_usage.py:31-180`; report command only prompt/completion/cost (`management/commands/llm_usage_report.py:21-60`), omits cached/reasoning in CSV. No authoritative price table; `cost_usd` is provider-reported/nullable. Cached-input billing cannot be derived from total tokens or cached_tokens alone without provider rate card and whether cached tokens are included in prompt_tokens; ask provider billing export/rate card + request/response usage fields.
Measured artifacts: prior doc `docs/product/measurements/2026-09-03-judge-thinking-passthrough.md` confirms seat2 extra_body no-think 945→72 completion, 870→0 reasoning, 34.8→2.9s; seat1 no-think recall loss, so reasoning-off is model-specific, not a generic optimization. Priority hypotheses: P0 measure per-request usage by seat/model/run with prompt/completion/cached/reasoning/cost + batch size; distinguish attempted/HTTP/parsed/paid. P1 reduce output: retain structured error essentials but cap descriptions/back_translation (quality risk: producer usability/recall); enforce max_tokens only after observed p95 and refusal/unparsed rate. Audit evidence: Phase0 sealed test is strongest human-ish holdout but one-shot, old aliases/models. docs/product/measurements/2026-08-13-phase0-measurements.md:345-370,388-395: 433 fr records (167 clean/146 major/120 critical), DeepSeek single H-recall 90.6 [86.5,93.6], H-specificity 98.2, R-recall 95.0, 3/120 critical->pass; Qwen 92.1/89.8/97.5; union max severity 97.4 H-recall, 98.3 R-recall, 0/120 critical pass but false flags 11.4%, auto-pass 72.9%. Model selection did not replicate (train/dev DeepSeek H recall 94.8 vs sealed 90.6; Qwen 87.9->92.1; McNemar p .0005 vs .20), so do not justify current seat choice from train/dev. Cascade is empirically rejected: same doc :205-233: best cascade recall 87.1 vs DeepSeek single 94.0; tier-B overturns 46/48 real defects in DS→Sonnet, 18/21 DS→Qwen; only Qwen→DS 16 correct/8 wrong but still 87.1. Full parallel/max-severity union is the only measured two-seat design with recall gain, but direct union reconstructed on train/dev; sealed union result is from persisted arms and not fresh current config.

Corpus bias/gaps: docs/product/designs/2026-08-26-balanced-judge-evaluation-corpus.md:18-49: 419/919 clean labels from two LLM annotators; their defect rates 29.6% vs 15.7%, zero unit overlap, only 2 critical/560; all 500 defects constructed. :51-62: instruments only ru→zh human (124, 7 critical), en→fr constructed (236), ru→fr constructed (919); one human-real language pair. Proposed 6-pair coverage (en-de/tr/ja/fa, ru-ko/zh) remains proposal :98-125. Model annotators reproduce blind spots: 9/14 human-confirmed defects below major (same doc :39-43; also index :485-487). Six-audit gaps in index :445-603: false-reject ≤2% un-certifiable with n=167 clean; per-language calibration only fr+zh, no novel domain; ordinal seat agreement no kappa (only binary overlap); repair-loop success unmeasured; day-to-day drift, batch/concurrency effects, human review time and production-scale cost unmeasured. Index :523-537,539-561,575-603.

Severity/threshold evidence: docs/product/measurements/2026-08-19-severity-recalibration-final.md:39-81,82-132,157-160: n=5 repeats × 2 seats × 3 prompt arms, 30/30 parsed; noise ≥flag 20-32% per seat/arm and 24-31% collegium; collegium baseline missed critical 1/7 median, false critical 5/124, C rubric 2/7 missed + 5 false critical; B description improves precision 0.51→0.54 but recall .75→.67, fails R1; C reduces noise 39→30/124 and reaches REAL 12/14 median but R2 fails (no arm catches all critical every repeat; false critical 4-5 > ≤2). Thus repair policy empirically unjustified; any cheaper repair/model needs offline validation.

Acceptance metrics for cheaper variants (recommend): frozen prompt/schema/profile + held-out human-labeled sets across at least existing zh plus new language/script strata; per-language critical recall lower CI bound >= incumbent release floor (historical target 88%, point >=95), no increase in critical→pass; clean false-critical upper CI <=2/124 (or explicitly redesign); H recall non-inferiority margin ≤2-3pp, false-flag upper bound agreed; parsed/unparsed 100% on bounded transport canary and p95/max within per-seat deadlines; repeat noise measured n≥5 with flip rate not worse than incumbent; disagreement/union must report weighted kappa and complementarity, not just overlap; cost measured via actual provider usage including reasoning tokens and full component scale. Current evidence supports seat2 no-think speed adoption only (if exact alias retained), rejects cascade/demotion and severity-only thresholds, and does not justify model swap/seat removal/repair change.

Important audit hygiene: judge-measurements-index.md's 'latency NOT MEASURED' section (around :4.1-4.2) is stale/contradicted by Sep production docs; cite current per-seat measurements instead, and mark index status as historical. Never compare OpenRouter historical quality/cost to LiteLLM current pair without paired same-profile offline evaluation; 2026-09-01-04 :51-75 says model, batch width, deadline differ and R3 forbids provider attribution. Current LiteLLM parsed/unparsed aggregate is confounded too: atlas/qwen 96 parsed/51 unparsed during a rollout 400 window, DeepSeek 97/0, versus later stable runs.

Suggested six-area audit framing grounded in repo: (1) Dataset/ground truth: constructed defects dominate; LLM-clean labels lack overlap/critical coverage; only zh has human inventory; add multi-language human adjudication and prevalence-stratified production sample. (2) Coverage/generalization: only ru→fr, en→fr, ru→zh; no novel domain, scripts, approved translations, or language transfer; six-pair proposal unexecuted. (3) Judge validity/reliability: sealed holdout shows non-replication; n=5 noise 20–32%; no weighted kappa/ordinal agreement; current aliases unvalidated. (4) Decision/rubric: severity thresholds fail R1/R2; union false flags 11.4%; critical false positives 4–5/124; repair outcomes unmeasured. (5) Systems/transport: current canaries prove parse/latency only; LiteLLM cost blind; Stage3 resets and alias changes confound old data; batch/concurrency/provider effects not isolated. (6) Economics/governance: historical OpenRouter per-1k costs are not current dollars; no full-scale/repair/review-time ROI; savings require fixed-profile offline non-inferiority then bounded canary, no automatic seat/model/repair changes from transport-only runs.

AI LQA https://docs.lokalise.com/en/articles/7945761-ai-lqa: batch existing translations, GPT API/DQF-MQM, glossary checks/reports/suggestions, consumes Pro AI words but not processed words, quota exhaustion locks task. Trados Smart Review docs https://docs.rws.com/en-US/trados-enterprise-accelerate-791599/smart-review-task-1253227 and https://docs.rws.com/en-US/trados-enterprise-accelerate-791605/using-translation-quality-estimation-1152353: automated batch or interactive LLM review, thresholds can lock/confirm > threshold; Smart Review (AWS Bedrock default, Azure options) and MTQE purchased separately contractually; task can mark Translation Approved/Rejected—unsafe direct fit for HCGameLoc advisory semantics. Language Weaver https://docs.rws.com/en-US/trados-studio-2022-980998/language-weaver-426803: included cloud packages/character allowance, dictionaries/terminology; no public current judge pricing. Local fit: HCGameLoc Django Weblate/Celery, cap 2000 and runs 3004/3031 HTTP attempts in prior evidence (docs/operations/measurements/2026-09-17-anvil-saga-judge-investigation.md:14-25, 167-193), judge is advisory/no 0–100 UI (weblate/trans/models/judge.py:1021-1054; weblate/trans/tests/test_judge_views.py:467-474), deterministic checks block.

Independent primary methodology: MQM Council https://www.themqm.org/mqm-pillars/the-mqm-scoring-models/ says evaluation may use selected samples or entire docs; common samples 500–20,000 words; implementers choose error types/specifications and determine sample size/procedure. MQM definition https://tranquality.info/mqm/mqm-spec-2014-02-14.html explicitly says MQM does not define one universal metric; a detected issue may be unconfirmed until human review, and user-selected issue subsets should match purpose. WMT/TACL study https://aclanthology.org/2021.tacl-1.87.pdf warns single-score isolated-sentence evaluation can hide errors/bias; explicit error listing is more informative, and their MQM raters use document context. Use this to reject vendor 0–100 score as a shipping truth: HCGameLoc can retain categorical advisory findings + deterministic checks, and use calibrated stratified sample for judge monitoring rather than evaluate all 57,996 rows.

Suggested decision framing: five vendor patterns, but recommend HCGameLoc hybrid rather than buying/imitating a 0–100 score. Strongest reusable controls: (1) deterministic checks/TM/glossary first; (2) cheap bounded judge sample (stratified by language/content/severity/history), then only flagged/uncertain rows to costly second pass or human; (3) hard per-run/day/month monetary + request budgets with reserve/stop and usage ledger; (4) categorical advisory outcomes only, never auto-approve/reject from model. Phrase/Lokalise scores and RWS approval states conflict with HC invariants; Smartling LQA Agent requires English source (Anvil source is Russian); Crowdin limits/BYOK + optional QA retry are best cost-safety pattern but AI Pipeline cascades can multiply calls; memoQ/RWS QE is mostly provider/contract gated. Smartling Plans publicly lists only starting translation rates ($0.0075 MT, $0.06 AI, $0.12 AI-human, $0.20 human), not LQE/LQA-specific rates—cite https://www.smartling.com/plans and avoid converting judge cost. Phrase has public AIU ratios and capacity restrictions, but no dollar rates. Crowdin minimum managed balance is $10; AI API docs expose $ daily/monthly/user limits; no universal per-word rate.
